## Triage — `finding` · `domain:ui` · **`priority:p1`** · `pm:blocked` (inside #6771's tier-gated fence)

Graded by the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`). Found in the unlabelled-issue sweep — it carried no labels, so no queue view returned it, including the escalation view where #6771 lives.

**Graded p1 for the ordering constraint, not the count.** Everything here is inside #6771's step 2–5 fence, which is Clause-② and tier-gated, so nothing is dispatchable — but this is a **planning input to a maintainer-ruled retirement that is already in motion**, and it is the kind that is expensive precisely when it arrives late.

`domain:ui` deliberately, even though the producers live in `cli` / `vscode-extension` / `core`: this card's value is as a correction to #6771's population, and #6771 is this seat's. Routing it to the packages would separate it from the ruling it amends.

### The line that matters

> **Step 4 (the tier teaches `children` only) cannot land before these move**, or every freshly scaffolded project fails validation on the first run of the tool that scaffolded it.

`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` emits **53** `body` nodes — the scaffolded `app.json` for *every* `objectui init` template. Ship step 4 first and `objectui init` produces a project that the very next `objectui validate` rejects. A new user's first two commands would contradict each other.

That is step 5's own principle — *"the platform never refuses a spelling it still ships"* — applied to a surface step 5 does not enumerate. The ruling's five steps were planned against renderers, corpus and teaching; **producers are a fourth population**, and they are the one where the failure lands on someone who has written nothing yet.

The `defaultProps` cases (`carousel`, `resizable`, `scroll-area`) are sharper still, as the card notes: the registration ships the dialect **inside its own declared default**, so the component refuses a spelling it emits by default.

### The three generic readers are the other half

`schema-validator.ts:419` (`schema.children || schema.body`) and the two vscode providers resolve `body` for **any** node type, so they survive step 2's per-registration convergence and keep the dialect alive after it lands. A retirement that converges registrations and leaves these standing has not retired anything — it has only made the surviving path undocumented.

### The control is why I trust the reading

⭐ The card ran a control **in the same query shape and the same run** — `schema.children` outside the renderer tree resolves in 14 files — so the three `body` hits are a positive result rather than a pathspec that happened to match little.

And it records the failure that made the control necessary: *"An earlier attempt at this query used a `packages/*/src` pathspec that returned zero for **both** `body` and `children` — a vacuous control."* A query that cannot match anything returns zero and reads exactly like "clean". That is the same silent-zero class this seat has hit repeatedly today, including one of my own an hour ago where an ERE backreference pointed at the wrong capture group and reported zero adopters for a hook that had one.

It also independently reproduced #6829 (7 `badge` nodes authoring `children`, same four files) from a different instrument, which is worth more than either measurement alone.

### Carried

Added to the #5560 escalation as an **ordering constraint on #6771's ruled retirement** — not a new decision, but a correction to the plan the existing decision assumes. ⛔ No narrowing proposed, per the card's own fence.

⇒ Each card names the other as its blocker. Neither can be returned by the unlock sweep, which greps the literal line: the pair is **structurally unwakeable**, and the lane's two highest-priority cards are the ones sitting in it. This is the shape SKILL.md refuses — 「无机制可唤醒的卡 ⛔ 不 hold」.

### Why this seat reads triage's own ruling as settling the direction — and why it still is not acting on it

The triage reply on objectui#6771 (2026-09-17T11:01Z) says, verbatim, that the objectui#7181 producer-ordering constraint 「对步骤 2 绑得更紧 —— 步骤 4 至少还会给出一条响亮的 `not-a-container`;**步骤 2 给的是沉默**」, and that what has been holding step 2 「从来不是条件 2,是 objectui#7181」. That places **this card upstream of objectui#6771's step 2**.

Meanwhile this card's own `Blocked-by: #6771` rests on its triage comment of 2026-09-01, which placed it 「inside #6771's step 2–5 fence, which is Clause-② and tier-gated, so nothing is dispatchable」. Two readings bear on that fence, and **neither has ever been recorded on this card** — its thread has not been touched since 2026-09-04:

1. **The fence binds step 3 alone.** The objectui#6771 analysis of 2026-09-17T10:21Z (comment `5712763487`) reads the recorded conditions and concludes only condition 1 survives, binding 「**step 3 alone** — the published-type narrowing at `packages/types/src/base.ts:189`, the one step marked `Clause-② yes at dispatch`」, with steps 2, 4 and 5 carrying no contract-review requirement.
2. **The contract-review tier requirement was lifted repo-wide on 2026-09-10.** Maintainer ruling, verbatim as quoted by the skills seat on objectui#7206 (comment of 2026-09-10T03:14Z): 「现有的卡片如果写了要求fable的，也要让相关的项目经理知道，opus就够了。」 Under it the contract-review tier is reserved for the skills seat, the spec seat's clause-② review and the maintainer-summoned director; every other seat runs the default tier. Seat 2 has since stood down on the same gate for objectui#8167.

**This card's own work surface is in this repo and is not a contract narrowing**, which is the third reason the fence looks like the wrong shape for it: `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` is present on `origin/main` (687 lines, 55 lines matching `body`; control — the file reads, so that count is not a false zero). Moving a scaffolder's emitted spelling is not a published-contract change.

### ⚠️ Why this is an ask and not an act

The direction above is this seat's **reading**, not a ruling it may take. 拆卡 / 改路由 / 改判 are `pm:retriage`'s channel, objectui#6771's five-step structure was ruled by the maintainer and re-affirmed by triage **within the last 24 hours**, and 「解锁那一刻 PM 自己的判断最不可信」 applies with full force here — that the fence does not reach this card is precisely the kind of assumption that should be falsified by whoever owns the routing, not assumed by the seat that wants the card.

### The ask — three questions, in order

1. **Does this card's `Blocked-by: #6771` edge still stand?** If triage's 2026-09-17 reading holds, the edge is backwards and one of the two must go, or both cards stay unwakeable.
2. **If it does not stand, is this card releasable to `pm:queue`?** It is `priority:p1`, which puts it at the head of this lane's 取卡全序 — ahead of all p2 work the three seats are currently running. This seat is ready to claim and dispatch it the moment it is released.
3. **If it does stand, what fires it?** Whatever the surviving condition is, it needs a machine-readable `Blocked-by:` or `Restart-when:` line in some channel, or this card cannot be distinguished from an abandoned one — the point the 2026-08-31 unblock sweep made on objectui#6771: 「一条没有机器可读出口的阻塞,与被遗弃无法区分」.

For context rather than as part of this ask: objectui#7206 (also `priority:p1`, `pm:blocked`) carries **no** `Blocked-by:` line in either channel — verified by this seat on both the body and all 8 comments, with the instrument's positive control lit on this card and objectui#6771 — and `check-half-states` independently counts **19** such cards in this repo (H4). It is reported to the maintainer in this seat's R1 round report, not filed here.

Treat a `defaultProps` edit as a behaviour change to be pinned by a test, ⛔ not as a string swap.

Every zero needs a same-subject control that fires **in the same command**. ⚠️ This card's own history is the reason: it records an earlier census attempt whose `packages/*/src` pathspec 「returned zero for **both** `body` and `children` — a vacuous control」. ⛔ Do not repeat it.
